paper_sections.title: The Temporal Dynamics of Voluntary Emotion Regulation
Modulation of the sustained by the immediate aftereffect

description.value: The study examined the immediate and delayed neural aftereffects of voluntary emotion regulation by detachment, focusing on amygdala responses during active regulation and subsequent passive viewing of the same aversive stimuli.

design.value: The study was composed of two tasks. During task 1 (“active regulation”), subjects either simply watched negative or neutral pictures and permitted their emotions or intentionally regulated their emotions by taking the position of a neutral observer. Approximately ten minutes after the end of task 1, task 2 (“passive viewing”) presented the same pictures again in a newly randomized order without instructions to regulate.

description.value: A measure used to rule out effects of altered mood states; two subjects with BDI scores above the cut-off score of 9 were discarded from further analyses.
An assessment of state and trait anxiety used to rule out effects of altered mood states.
A measure used to rule out deficits in emotion perception.
A questionnaire assessing habitual emotion regulation strategies, including suppression and reappraisal subscales.
A measure of habitual thought control, included to test whether it modulated potential aftereffects of emotion regulation.
Post-hoc rating of emotion regulation success, with 1 indicating very successful and 9 indicating not successful.

description.value: A 0-to-7 rating of subjective negative affect used in the independent control experiment, where 0 was weakest and 7 strongest.

Task 2 tested passive viewing of pictures that had formerly been regulated or not regulated in task 1.

name.value: peak magnitude of the immediate aftereffect

source_definition.value: The difference score between scan 9 regulation and scan 9 no regulation.

description.value: 20 healthy right-handed female volunteers aged 24±3 years without any history of neurological or psychiatric illness participated in the imaging study; two subjects were discarded from further analyses, leaving 18 subjects included in the analyses.

exclusion_criteria.value: any history of neurological or psychiatric illness
BDI scores above the cut-off score of 9

medical_condition.value: No history of neurological or psychiatric illness

clinical_characteristics.value: All 18 subjects included in the analyses had average (non pathological) scores on the BDI, STAI and TAS-20.

description.value: An independent sample (n=10) completed a control experiment using a trial-by-trial rating of subjective negative affect.

task_description.value: Subjects saw 60 pictures of negative or neutral content. They were instructed either to simply watch the pictures and permit all upcoming emotions or to intentionally regulate their emotions by taking the position of a neutral observer. The instruction was presented as a cue word for 2 s, picture presentation lasted 8 s, and subjects then relaxed for 20 s without regulating any more. Trials were presented in randomized order, and task 1 was performed in two consecutive sessions of 15 minutes each.

instructions.value: For regulation: “Look at the following picture directly but try to take the position of a noninvolved observer, thinking about the present picture in a neutral way.” For no regulation: “Look at the following picture directly and permit feeling your emotions.” After picture presentation, subjects were instructed to not regulate any more and relax.

stimuli.value: 60 pictures of negative or neutral content taken from the International Affective Picture System and matched for complexity and content of faces, scenery, food and nature.

task_performance_measures.value: Post-hoc emotion regulation success on a 9-point-Likert scale

task_description.value: Approximately ten minutes after the end of task 1, subjects looked at the same 60 pictures again. The pictures were presented for only 1 s each in a newly randomized order to minimize intentional emotion regulation efforts. The intertrial interval was 3 s with a variable jitter within ±1 TR.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to just look at the 60 pictures again; no instructions to regulate were given.

stimuli.value: The same 60 International Affective Picture System pictures used in task 1.

task_description.value: An independent sample of 10 subjects completed a control experiment using a trial-by-trial rating of subjective negative affect to confirm the success of the emotion regulation procedure.

task_performance_measures.value: Trial-by-trial rating of subjective negative affect, from 0 (weakest) to 7 (strongest)

modality.value: T2* weighted functional MR images using event-related echoplanar imaging

instrument.value: 3 Tesla Siemens Allegra scanner equipped with a head coil

description.value: Functional images were obtained in a tangential-axial orientation using an imaginary line from the orbitofrontal cortex to the cerebellum to minimize susceptibility artifacts. Image size was 64×64 pixels, field of view was 192 mm, and flip angle was 90°. One whole-brain volume consisted of 31 slices. Slice thickness was 3 mm with a 25% gap. Volumes were obtained every 2000 ms with TE 35 ms.

modality.value: T2* weighted functional MR images using event-related echoplanar imaging

instrument.value: 3 Tesla Siemens Allegra scanner equipped with a head coil

description.value: In task 2, volumes were obtained every 1500 ms with TE 35 ms. One volume consisted of 23 slices with a slice thickness of 3 mm and a 25% gap, covering the brain from the temporal poles to the superior parietal cortex and including the amygdala, prefrontal cortex and parietal cortex. All other acquisition parameters were similar to task 1.

instrument.value: 3 Tesla Siemens Allegra scanner equipped with a head coil

description.value: For each subject, three-dimensional T1 weighted anatomical volumes were acquired.
Data preprocessing and statistical analyses were carried out with SPM 2 and Matlab 6.5.1 and were similar for both tasks.

steps.value: spatial normalization to the EPI-template (2×2×2 mm)

model_settings.value: The regression model consisted of five regressors: instruction, non-regulated negative, non-regulated neutral, regulated negative, and regulated neutral, plus six regressors describing residual motion. Intrinsic autocorrelations were accounted for by an autoregressive model of 1 order and low frequency drifts were removed via high pass filter.

Second level random effects group analysis comparing individual regionally specific effects of conditions for each subject using a 2×2 design with the factors regulation condition (regulation, no regulation) and valence (negative, neutral), with non-sphericity correction resulting in a t-statistic for every voxel.

Mean amygdala time courses for each subject and each condition were analyzed with factors valence, regulation and period. Data were taken from scan 5, 6 s after picture onset, and scan 9, 6 s after picture offset.
Regression of extracted individual data for the contrast regulation negative>no-regulation negative in DLPFC with the contrast no-regulation negative>regulation negative in left and right amygdala.
Correlation of individual WBSI scores with the peak magnitude of the immediate aftereffect, defined as the difference score between scan 9 regulation and scan 9 no regulation.

Regression testing whether amygdala activation during presentation of formerly regulated negative pictures in task 2 covaried with individual differences in peak immediate aftereffect magnitude in task 1.
Trial-by-trial subjective negative affect was compared between regulated negative trials and non-regulated negative trials.
